long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Shanghai, Michael R. Hsing came to the United States at 21, supported himself through university and earned an electrical-engineering degree from Florida. After developing and patenting power-semiconductor technologies at analog chipmakers, he founded Monolithic Power Systems in 1997. His aim was to integrate complete power-management functions onto a single chip, and he led MPS through its public offering in 2004. The business expanded into data-center, automotive, communications, industrial and consumer applications.

Hsing remains MPS chairman, president and chief executive, combining technical-founder continuity with responsibility for strategy and product direction. The latest proxy reports beneficial ownership of about 2.1 percent, including shares held directly and through trusts. That position establishes a substantial personal equity interest but not majority voting control; several institutional investors report larger stakes. MPS revenue, assets and market capitalization belong to the listed company. They should not be treated as Hsing's personal holdings, while current net-worth estimates remain inherently time-sensitive.
